Tasks.TaskName: Step 3: From DMZ to OFFICE network

?.MaxConcurrentActions: (Mandatory) Maximum number of 'Actions' to run in parallel, 'Tasks' are always run sequentially. Possible values: 1 - Run one action at a time, this is the default; 5 - Run 5 actions in parallel; 10 - Run 10 actions in parallel; ...

Tasks.TaskName: (Mandatory) Name of the task. Used in the email and log files.

Sftp.ComputerName: (Mandatory) The name of the computer where the SFTP server is running.

Credential.UserName: (Mandatory) SFTP user name. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SFTP_USERNAME').
Credential.Password: (Mandatory 'Password' or 'PasswordKeyFile') SFTP password. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SFTP_PASSWORD').
Credential.PasswordKeyFile: (Mandatory 'Password' or 'PasswordKeyFile') Path to the SFTP password key file used to authenticate to the SFTP server. This is an SSH private key file in the OpenSSH format. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SFTP_PASSWORD_KEY_FILE').

Sftp.Port: (Optional) The TCP port number used to connect to the SFTP server. Defaults to 22 if not specified.

Option.OverwriteFile: (Mandatory) Specifies whether to overwrite duplicate files in the destination folder. Possible values: true - Overwrite duplicate files; false - Do not overwrite duplicate files and log an error.
Option.MatchFileNameRegex: (Mandatory) A regular expression to match file names. Possible values: '.*' - Process all files; '\.xlsx$' - Process only Excel files; 'Report_[0-9]{8}\.xlsx$' - Process only files with names starting with 'Report_' and ending with '.xlsx' followed by 8 digits; ...

Actions.ComputerName: (Mandatory) The name of the computer where the SFTP commands will be run. Ensure the 'Posh-SSH' PowerShell module is installed on this machine. Possible values: 'SERVER1' - A remote server name; 'localhost' - The local system.

Paths.Source: (Mandatory) The path to the source folder. Possible values: 'sftp:\path' - A string that starts with 'sftp:\' representing a folder on the SFTP server defined in 'Sftp.ComputerName'; 'c:\path' - A string representing a folder on the file system in 'Actions.ComputerName'.
Paths.Destination: (Mandatory) The path to the destination folder. Possible values: 'sftp:\path' - A string that starts with 'sftp:\' representing a folder on the SFTP server defined in 'Sftp.ComputerName'; 'c:\path' - A string representing a folder on the file system in 'Actions.ComputerName'.

?.PSSessionConfiguration: (Optional) The PowerShell version of the remote endpoint. This value corresponds to the output of the Get-PSSessionConfiguration cmdlet. The minimum supported version is 'PowerShell.7'. Defaults to 'PowerShell.7' if not specified.

Settings.ScriptName: (Mandatory) Name of the script, used in the log files and in the event logs.

SendMail.When: (Mandatory) Specifies when to send an email notification. Possible values: 'OnError' - Send email only when a system error or an action error occurs; 'OnErrorOrAction' - Send email when the script performed actions or when errors occurred; 'Always' - Send email when the script is finished, regardless of success or failure; 'Never' - Do not send email.
SendMail.From: (Mandatory) The sender's email address. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS').
SendMail.FromDisplayName: (Optional) The display name to show for the sender. Email clients may display this differently. It is most likely to be shown if the sender's email address is not recognized (e.g., not in the address book). Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:MAIL_FROM_DISPLAY_NAME').
SendMail.To: (Mandatory 'To' or 'Bcc') An array of recipient email addresses. The script will send an email to all addresses in the array.
SendMail.Bcc: (Mandatory 'To' or 'Bcc') An array of BCC email addresses.
SendMail.Subject: (Optional) The subject line of the email. Default value: 'N actions, N errors'
SendMail.Body: (Optional) The HTML body of the email. Default value: A summary table with action and error count.

Smtp.ServerName: (Mandatory) The hostname or IP address of the SMTP server. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SMTP_SERVER').
Smtp.Port: (Mandatory) The port number of the SMTP server. Possible values: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SMTP_PORT').
Smtp.ConnectionType: (Optional) The connection type for the SMTP server. Possible values: 'None' - No encryption; 'Auto' - Attempt TLS, fall back to unencrypted; 'SslOnConnect' - Use SSL from the beginning; 'StartTls' - Start with unencrypted, then upgrade to TLS; 'StartTlsWhenAvailable' - Start with unencrypted, upgrade to TLS if supported. Default value: 'None'. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SMTP_CONNECTION_TYPE').
Smtp.UserName: (Optional) The username for authenticating with the SMTP server. If undefined or NULL, no authentication is attempted. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SMTP_USERNAME').
Smtp.Password: (Optional) The password for authenticating with the SMTP server. If undefined or NULL, no authentication is attempted. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:SMTP_PASSWORD').

AssemblyPath.?: To use email functionality, install the following packages: 'Install-Package -Name 'MailKit' Source 'https://www.nuget.org/api/v2' Scope 'AllUsers' -SkipDependencies' - 'Install-Package -Name 'MimeKit' Source 'https://www.nuget.org/api/v2' Scope 'AllUsers' -SkipDependencies'
AssemblyPath.MailKit: (Mandatory) Path to the MailKit.dll assembly. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:MAILKIT_ASSEMBLY').
AssemblyPath.MimeKit: (Mandatory) Path to the MimeKit.dll assembly. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:MIMEKIT_ASSEMBLY').

What.SystemErrors: (Mandatory) Whether to log execution errors, incorrect input file errors, etc. Possible values: true or false.
What.AllActions: (Mandatory) Whether to log all actions performed by the script, including errors. Possible values: true or false.
What.OnlyActionErrors: (Mandatory) Whether to log only actions that failed. Possible values: true or false.

Where.Folder: (Mandatory) The path to the folder where log files will be created. Value '..\Logs': Path relative to the script. Value 'C:\MyApp\Logs': An absolute path. If not specified or NULL, no log files will be created. Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:LOG_FOLDER').
Where.FileExtensions: (Mandatory) An array of file extensions for the log files (e.g., ['.csv'], ['.json'], ['.txt'], ['.xlsx']). Multiple values are supported. Ignored when Folder is NULL. To use '.xlsx', install the following PowerShell modules 'Install-Module ImportExcel'.

SaveLogFiles.DeleteLogsAfterDays: (Optional) The number of days to keep log files. Log files older than this value (based on their last write time) will be removed from the log folder specified in 'SaveLogFiles.Where.Folder'. If not specified or 0, logs will be kept indefinitely. CAUTION: Ensure the 'SaveLogFiles.Where.Folder' is specifically designated for log files to avoid unintended deletion of other files.

SaveInEventLog.Save: (Mandatory) Whether to log messages to the Windows event log. Possible values: true or false.
SaveInEventLog.LogName: (Mandatory) The name of the event log to write to (e.g., 'Application', 'System', or a custom log name like 'Scripts'). Supports environment variables (e.g., 'ENV:EVENT_LOG_NAME').
